title: Read the failures, not the average
statement: After every change, read the failing items and compare them with the baseline's item by item, because an unchanged average or pass rate can hide new failures.
example: A new version fixed all 9 of the old one's failures and failed 11 new items, with no item failing in both.
detail: When one AP model was retrained, its pass rate fell from 85.0% to 81.7%, two items on its set, yet no item failed in both versions: the new one fixed all 9 of the old one's failures and introduced 11 new ones (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`). On another day, reading the failures showed all 26 were content failures with no parse failure among them, so the plan recorded that three fixes aimed at output format and examples had all addressed the wrong failure mode (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/FINAL_PLAN_2026_05_11_v3.md`). Read the checks each failing item failed, and compare before naming a cause: an unchanged total can hide a new kind of failure or an item type that broke.
against: the same notes say not every failure needs a full root-cause investigation. The new failures were two items each, few enough that they may be run-to-run variation rather than a real change. At 15 items the source puts its noise floor at about one item per type, so differences by type are directional only.
